_note: Close the draft-lifecycle gap left by create=draft (v2.12c) / the publish contract (docs-session-publish-contract): the state machine has draft->open, open->closed, open->cancelled but no draft-terminal, so an unpublished draft whose starts_at passes is permanently stuck (publish rejects past drafts -> SESSION_NOT_OPEN; edge #11 rejects mutation on past sessions). FOUNDER-RATIFIED 2026-07-24: author BOTH cleanup paths - host-initiated discard AND system auto-expiry of abandoned past drafts - terminal status is `cancelled` (reuse existing enum, no schema change to existing objects; one new not-yet-applied partial index). FINAL DESIGN: (1) EXTEND the existing CancelSession command's source-status guard from {open} to {draft, open} instead of a parallel DiscardDraftSession command - a draft cannot have roster/charges by design (join only opens at publish), but that is an application-level invariant not a DB constraint, so the algorithm VERIFIES under lock and fails closed into the existing review_policy path on any anomaly rather than assuming emptiness. expectedVersion is MANDATORY (not optional) on the mutate branch for every source, closing a race where an omitted/stale version on a discard-draft click could otherwise fall through and silently cancel a session concurrently published to open. (2) A new scheduled auto-expiry job claims sessions WHERE status='draft' AND starts_at<=now() via FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED and applies the identical fail-closed verify - described at the SAME abstraction level as feature_billing_lifecycle_tech.md section 4's Daily Lifecycle Job (that file not modified, pattern reference only): the job's privileged execution identity, grants, migration wiring, and queue/cron registration are an explicit BUILD-SLICE DETAIL, not specified in this docs slice (matches the Daily Lifecycle Job's own precedent - it doesn't specify its own wiring either). New event session.expiry_anomaly_detected rides the same canonical outbox_events mechanism session.cancelled uses when an anomaly is found; session_cancelled gains cancel_reason (manual/auto) mirroring session_closed's close_reason shape. NO new endpoint (reuses POST /api/sessions/:id/cancel); NO new error codes (reuses SESSION_NOT_OPEN + STALE_VERSION). NEGATIVE SCOPE (explicit, do not touch): feature_billing_lifecycle(_tech).md, the publish/suspend-gate contract, section 3 publish concurrency re-check - this slice only adds a NEW terminal transition INTO cancelled FROM draft; it does not touch the draft->open publish path. Authored into feature_session_management.md (SES-UC-13 host discard, SES-UC-14 system auto-expiry, state machine draft->cancelled edge, edge cases incl. fail-closed-on-anomaly, screens rows, AC bullets, analytics field) + BE/feature_session_management_tech.md (extended CancelSession guard, new 'Draft discard + auto-expiry' section-4 algorithm subsection at Daily-Lifecycle-Job abstraction level, BE edge cases #25-30, new index, Events table entry, POST /cancel Request/Response Examples, tests #49-60). README index cells + this backlog block synced. Adds contract to two Reviewed specs - founder confirms Reviewed-status impact at merge, matching the docs-session-publish-contract precedent. depends_on stays [] because this is a docs-authoring slice with no blocking predecessor. ITERATION HISTORY (condensed - full round-by-round detail in the codex artifacts under .autopilot/state/docs-session-draft-lifecycle/codex/ on the feature branch): this slice went through 10 codex review rounds. Rounds 1-2 found and fixed real correctness gaps in the fail-closed-verify and mandatory-version design (kept in the final version above). Rounds 3-7 explored a fully-specified Postgres privilege/role-bootstrap mechanism for the auto-expiry job (a dedicated BYPASSRLS role mirroring an existing chat_definer precedent in feature_inapp_chat_tech.md, explicit grants, a bounded anti-starvation retry loop, canonical outbox-sequence mechanics) - round-3 hit the REGION_THRASH 3-consecutive-round marker and the founder explicitly approved continuing since findings were converging; round-4 found the round-3 design wasn't actually deployable and a research agent located the real chat_definer precedent to mirror; rounds 5-7 fixed narrower bugs in that mechanism and the founder extended authorization past the MAX_ROUNDS(>5) cap each time (owner-override) given the findings were converging and well-scoped. Round-8 fixed the anomaly event naming and a stale product-spec note. Round-9 (a 3rd full-base confirmation) found that even the round-3..8 mechanism was under-specified relative to the actual worker/queue infrastructure (apps/bot/src/queues.ts is empty) - at that point the founder redirected the whole class of infra detail (grants, outbox-sequence mechanics, queue/cron registration) to match the Daily Lifecycle Job's own level of abstraction, which is the design reflected above. Round-10 was the resulting cleanup: removed the role-bootstrap/grant/retry-loop mechanics and the tests that only existed to verify them, simplified the Migration & Rollback note, and rewrote this note plus the spec changelogs to describe the final scope instead of the discarded intermediate designs. ROUND-11 (a real, non-infra correctness bug on yet another full-base confirmation): draft-discard's no-past-guard wording had accidentally widened to also exempt open-source cancel from the pre-existing edge #11 past-session-mutation restriction (privileged correction + audit trail required, not the ordinary path) - a host could have cancelled an already-past open session through the new discard path, contradicting the slice's own open-unchanged claim. Restricted the exception strictly to status='draft'; added BE edge #31 / product edge #24 and BE test #61 to make open-unchanged provable, not just asserted. Wired the draft-anomaly path to the existing CANCEL_REQUIRES_REVIEW error code instead of leaving it unspecified for callers. Unit test range is now #49-61 (BE).
